name: Bahrain (Behrain)
summary: Riverside town at the confluence of the Daral and Swat rivers, with handicraft markets and the trailhead for Daral and Saidgai lakes.

facts.text: The name means 'two rivers' for the Daral/Swat confluence.
facts.quote: due to its location at the confluence of the Daral and Swat rivers

facts.text: It is a base camp for the Daral and Saidgai lakes trail.
facts.quote: It also serves as a base camp for the trail that leads to the Daral and Saidgai lakes.

access: N-95, 60 km north of Mingora; year-round road.

name: Barikot
summary: Gateway town to central Swat and base for the Bazira, Gumbat, Shingardar and Amluk-Dara sites.

facts.text: Barikot lies on the middle course of the Swat River, about 20 km from Mingora.
facts.quote: It is located about 20 km (12 mi) away from Mingora and the Butkara Stupa.

access: N-95 from Chakdara/Mingora.

name: Daral Lake
summary: Amoeba-shaped glacial lake above Bahrain with a shepherds' mosque near its shore.

facts.text: It is at 3,505 m and only accessible in summer.
facts.quote: Daral Lake is accessible only during the summer

facts.text: A shepherds' mosque stands near the lake.
facts.quote: Near the lake, there is an ancient mosque where shepherds and visitors offer their prayers

access: Trek 4-5 h from Gabin Jabba or 3-4 h from Bahrain; June-Sept.

name: Dir (Dir Khas)
summary: Former capital of Dir state and Upper Dir seat, at the foot of Lowari Pass on the road to Chitral; the road to Kumrat leaves the main road here.

facts.text: At the base of Lowarai Pass on the road to Chitral.
facts.quote: It is at the base of the Lowarai Pass, the main road to Chitral.

facts.text: Founded in the 17th century.
facts.quote: Dir was founded in the 17th century.

access: N-45 from Chakdara/Timergara.

name: Fatehpur (Swat)
summary: Union council and small town on the Swat valley road between Madyan and Khwazakhela.

facts.text: Fatehpur is a union council of Upper Swat.
facts.quote: Fatehpur is an administrative unit, known as Union council, of Upper Swat District in the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province of Pakistan.

access: On the main Swat valley road (N-95) north of Mingora.

name: Kanju
summary: Village on the Swat River just north of Mingora, known for peaches and for the Ayub Bridge river views; Saidu Sharif airport sits beside it.

facts.text: Kanju lies 3 km from Mingora.
facts.quote: It is 3 kilometres away from Mingora, the main city of Swat District, and about 5 kilometres from Saidu Sharif, the district's capital.

facts.text: Kanju peaches are widely known.
facts.quote: The peaches of Kanju and overall Swat are known all over Pakistan.

access: On the Mingora-Kalam road.

name: Khwazakhela
summary: Second-largest commercial centre of Swat after Mingora, where shoppers from Kalam, Kohistan and Shangla come to trade; junction town for the Shangla road.

facts.text: Second-largest commercial centre in Swat.
facts.quote: Khwazakhela is the second-largest commercial center in Swat after Mingora.

facts.text: Draws people from Kalam, Kohistan and Shangla.
facts.quote: Many people from Kalam, Kohistan, and Shangla come here for shopping and business.

access: On the N-95 between Mingora and Madyan; all-year road.

name: Madyan
summary: Bustling Torwali-majority riverside town where the Chail and Swat valleys join; a dining and shopping stop and base for the Bahrain-Kalam road.

facts.text: Madyan is primarily inhabited by Torwalis.
facts.quote: Madyan is primarily inhabited by Torwalis.

facts.text: The Chail and Swat valleys join at Madyan.
facts.quote: The two valleys join at Madyan, 8 km below Bahrain.

access: N-95 about 55 km from Mingora.

name: Manglawar (Manglor)
summary: Town at the mouth of the Malam Jabba road, earlier a capital of the Swat state, with Buddhist reliefs and a stupa in its side valleys.

facts.text: Manglawar is a former capital of the Kingdom of Swat.
facts.quote: of Swat District in the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province of Pakistan and former capital of Kingdom of Swat.

access: 12 km from Saidu Sharif; junction for Malam Jabba and Jahanabad.

name: Miandam
summary: Forested hill-station valley west of the Swat River at the foot of the Hindu Kush, with a WWF medicinal-plant project.

facts.text: It is about 55 km from Mingora.
facts.quote: It is located at a distance of 55 km away from Mingora the capital of Swat Valley

facts.text: A WWF project promotes sustainable harvesting of medicinal plants.
facts.quote: the town is the site of a World Wide Fund for Nature project promoting sustainable harvesting of medicinal plants

access: Paved road from Madyan/Mingora side; spring-autumn, snow in winter.

name: Mingora
summary: The largest city of Swat and the district capital, on the Swat River. It is the base for the Butkara and Saidu Sharif Buddhist sites and the gateway for trips up-valley to Fizagat, Malam Jabba, Madyan and Kalam.

facts.text: Mingora is the largest city of Malakand Division.
facts.quote: Mingora is the largest city and the epicenter of social, cultural, and economic activities in Malakand Division

access: Main road hub; Swat Expressway/N-95 from Chakdara (about 40 km).

name: Saidu Sharif
summary: Former capital quarter of the princely state of Swat, adjoining Mingora; named after the Akhund of Swat (Saidu Baba). The state-era royal buildings, Jahanzeb College and the Swat Museum cluster here.

timeline.event: Settlement renamed Saidu Sharif (earlier Baligram) after Saidu Baba

facts.text: The older name was Baligram.
facts.quote: The older name of Saidu Sharif was Baligram.

facts.text: It is named for Saidu Baba.
facts.quote: It was named after Saidu Baba, a prominent leader of the former state of Swat.

access: Contiguous with Mingora.

name: Timergara
summary: Lower Dir district headquarters on the Panjkora, a transit town on the Chakdara-Dir road (N-45).

facts.text: Lies at 823 m on the east bank of the Panjkora.
facts.quote: Timergara city is located on the east bank of the Panjkora River. It lies at an altitude of 823 metres (2,700 ft).

access: N-45, between Chakdara and Dir.

name: Udegram (Odigram, ancient Ora)
summary: Village on the Swat River NW of Mingora on the site identified with Ora of Alexander's campaign, later a Hindu Shahi capital; hosts the Raja Gira castle and Ghaznavid mosque.

timeline.event: Alexander storms Odigram (Ora)
Hindu Shahi dynasty has its capital at Udigram

facts.text: Odigram is the site of the Ghaznavid-era mosque.
facts.quote: Odigram is the site of the Mahmud Ghaznavi Mosque, one of the oldest in Pakistan.

facts.text: Hindu Shahis made their capital at Udigram.
facts.quote: who made their capital at Udigram in lower Swat

access: 8 km NW of Mingora by road.

name: Amluk-Dara Stupa
summary: A large dome-shaped Buddhist stupa south of the Swat River, among the best-preserved in the valley, with a squarish plinth under a hemispherical dome visible for miles.

timeline.event: Stupa built
Discovered by Aurel Stein
Studied by Domenico Faccenna

facts.text: It was found by Aurel Stein in 1926.
facts.quote: The stupa was first discovered by a Hungarian-British archaeologist Sir Aurel Stein in 1926.

facts.text: The dome is 21 m across and 7 m tall.
facts.quote: a hemispherical dome measuring 7 meter in height and 21 meters in diameter

facts.text: It is unprotected and damaged by treasure hunters.
facts.quote: it is unprotected and is being damaged by treasure seekers.

access: South side of the river near Barikot/Shamozai; road then short walk.

name: Bazira (Barikot Ghundai)
summary: The excavated ancient city at Barikot hill, identified with the Bazira stormed by Alexander in 327 BCE. Italian excavations since 1984 show occupation from the Bronze Age, a fortified city from the mid-first millennium BCE, an Indo-Greek wall and later Kushan and Buddhist phases.

timeline.event: First traces of human presence (pit remains)
Early-historic fortified town
Alexander the Great takes Bazira (identification with Barikot)
Italian Archaeological Mission (ISMEO) excavations

facts.text: The Italian mission has excavated Bazira since 1984.
facts.quote: has been excavating ruins of the ancient town of Bazira under Barikot since 1984.

facts.text: Greek accounts of Alexander's 327 BCE attack are identified with Odigram (Ora) and Barikot (Bazira).
facts.quote: in Greek accounts, these towns are identified as Ora and Bazira, respectively.

facts.text: The fortified urban settlement dates to about the mid-first millennium BCE.
facts.quote: the fortified urban settlement in Barikot (lower area and acropolis) was established around mid-first millennium BC.

access: Barikot, about 20 km SW of Mingora on the main road; hill site reachable on foot from the road.

name: Butkara I Stupa
summary: The largest excavated Buddhist stupa of the Swat plain, on the eastern edge of Mingora near Saidu Sharif. A core stupa of the Mauryan/early Indo-Greek period was encased five times by later enlargements and ringed by hundreds of votive stupas. Italian excavations from 1956 recovered much of the Gandharan sculpture now in the Swat Museum.

timeline.event: Original stupa built; later enlarged five times by encasing the earlier structure
Italian Archaeological Mission led by Domenico Faccenna excavates the stupa

facts.text: The stupa was probably built in the 2nd century BCE, with a possible Ashokan origin.
facts.quote: It may have been built by the Mauryan emperor Ashoka, but it is generally dated slightly later to the 2nd century BCE.

facts.text: It was enlarged five times, each time by building over the previous structure.
facts.quote: The stupa was enlarged on five occasions during the following centuries

facts.text: Excavation by an Italian mission began in 1956.
facts.quote: led by archaeologist Domenico Faccenna from 1956

facts.text: The oldest core layer contained a coin of Chandragupta Maurya, supporting an early date.
facts.quote: The oldest core strata (GSt 1) revealed a coin of Chandragupta Maurya

access: Within Mingora/Saidu Sharif, about 1 km east of the Swat Museum; reachable by road year-round (flat, no hike).

name: Butkara III Stupa (minor stupa site)
summary: A smaller Buddhist stupa area with votive stupas, excavated in the same Italian programme as Butkara I and located about 1 km south-east of it, on the Mingora outskirts.
access: Mingora outskirts; short road access, no hike.

photos.attribution: Photo: Zarghun11, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

name: Chakdara Fort
summary: British-built hill fort commanding the Swat River crossing at the south entrance to Swat, on the site of an older Mughal fort and famed for its defence in 1897.

timeline.event: Mughals build a fort at Chakdara
British occupy and build the present fort
Besieged during the Siege of Malakand

facts.text: The Mughals built a fort in 1586; the British built the present one in 1896.
facts.quote: The Mughals built a fort here in 1586, occupied in 1895 by the British, who built the present fort in 1896

facts.text: It was besieged in 1897.
facts.quote: The Battle of Chakdara was a battle and siege of a British military fort by rebel Pashtun tribesmen during the Siege of Malakand

access: Chakdara, on the road from Malakand to Swat; fort is a military site, view from outside.

photos.attribution: Photo: Salmannadim, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

name: Elum Ghar (Mount Ilam)
summary: The prominent pyramid-like mountain on the Swat/Buner border south of Mingora, a historic Hindu pilgrimage site and the backdrop to Marghazar.

timeline.event: Hindu pilgrimage site (Ram Takht)

facts.text: It is the highest peak in the region, 2,800 m.
facts.quote: Elum Ghar is the highest peak in the region, and is snow-covered most of the year.

facts.text: It was a significant Hindu pilgrimage site until 1947.
facts.quote: The mountain was a significant pilgrimage site for Hindus until 1947

access: Hike from Marghazar/Pir Baba side; 1-day trek, local guide advised.

name: Ghalegay Buddha (rock relief)
summary: A Buddha figure carved in rock beside the main road near Ghalegay, with cave remains alongside.

facts.text: A Buddha is carved in rock beside the road to Mingora.
facts.quote: On the way to Mingora there is a statue of Buddha sculptured in a rock on the right side of G.T. road.

access: Roadside on the Mingora-Barikot road.

name: Gogdara Rock Carvings
summary: Prehistoric/early-historic rock engravings in the Gogdara valley near Udegram.
access: Near Udegram; local guide helpful.

name: Gumbat Stupa (Balo Kale)
summary: A well-preserved Buddhist stupa in the Kandak valley west of Barikot, listed in Wikidata as Gumbat Stupa.
access: West of Barikot along the Kandak valley road; short walk.

photos.attribution: Photo: SpeakingArch, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
Photo: SpeakingArch, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

name: Jahanabad Buddha (Manglawar rock relief)
summary: A colossal seated Buddha relief carved in a rock face in the Jahanabad side valley of Manglawar, in a style compared with Tang-era sculpture; its face was damaged by explosives in 2007 and later restored by Italian conservators.

timeline.event: Relief carved (stylistic dating only)
Attack with explosives damaged the head

facts.text: Its style is compared to 7th-8th century Tang sculpture.
facts.quote: the relief carving may be compared to 7th - 8th century Tang sculpture in central Asia.

facts.text: The head was damaged by explosives in 2007 and later restored.
facts.quote: In 2007 the Taliban tried to destroy the head of the relief with explosives

access: Jahanabad, ~7 km up the Malam Jabba road from Manglawar; steps up to the rock.

name: Mahmud Ghaznavi Mosque (Udegram)
summary: Excavated ruin of one of the earliest datable mosques in northern Pakistan: a rectangular hypostyle prayer hall with stone column bases, founded in 1048-49 CE according to an Arabic inscription naming a Ghaznavid general.

timeline.event: Mosque founded by Amir Nustagin per inscription
Foundation inscription found
Italian excavation

facts.text: The inscription records a mosque founded in 1048-49 by a Ghaznavid general.
facts.quote: The inscription attests to the foundation of a mosque in HE 440 (1048–49 CE) ordered by Amir Nustagin, a Ghaznavid General

facts.text: Excavation 1985-1999 uncovered a hypostyle mosque.
facts.quote: brought to light a hypostyle mosque with supports originally in wood

facts.text: The plan is rectangular, 28 m by 21 m.
facts.quote: is rectangular in plan, measuring 28m by 21m

access: Udegram, on the lower slope below Raja Gira Castle; short walk from the village road.

name: Nimogram Stupa
summary: A Buddhist stupa at Nimogram on the western side of lower Swat.
access: West of Chakdara/Barikot; local road.

photos.attribution: Photo: Morningpost, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

name: Raja Gira Castle (Udegram)
summary: Ruined hilltop fortification above Udegram (Odigram), tied by local tradition to the Hindu ruler Raja Gira defeated by Mahmud of Ghazni's forces; the Ghaznavid-era mosque lies on its lower slope.

timeline.event: Raja Gira attacked by Mahmud of Ghazni
Ghaznavid inscription found below the castle

facts.text: Local tradition: Raja Gira was attacked by Mahmud of Ghazni.
facts.quote: In the 11th century, according to the local traditions, the Hindu king Raja Gira and his subjects were attacked by Mahmud of Ghazni during one of his campaigns.

facts.text: An Arabic inscription was found on the slope below the castle.
facts.quote: In 1984 an inscription in Arabic engraved on a black marble was found by chance on the slopes of the hill below the castle of Raja Gira.

access: Udegram, about 8 km NW of Mingora; steep climb on foot.

name: Saidu Sharif I Stupa and Monastery
summary: A two-terrace Buddhist sacred area on the hillside above Saidu Sharif, consisting of a main stupa with minor stupas and viharas on the lower terrace and a monastery above. Excavated by the Italian mission, it is a key site for the early Gandharan art of Swat.

timeline.event: First building period with symmetrical layout
Italian Archaeological Mission excavations (pause 1966-1977)

facts.text: Excavation ran 1963-1982 with a long pause.
facts.quote: The excavations were initiated by the Italian Archaeological Mission in 1963 and ended in 1982, with a pause between 1966 and 1977.

facts.text: The sacred area has two terraces with a stupa and a monastery.
facts.quote: The sacred area consists of two terraces built on the slope of the hill

facts.text: The first period dates from 25 BCE to the end of the 1st century.
facts.quote: between 25 BCE and the end of the 1st century

access: Edge of Saidu Sharif town, short walk from the road; year-round.

name: Shingardar Stupa
summary: A large Buddhist stupa of slate and stone near Ghalegay, between Mingora and Barikot, traditionally linked to king Uttarasena's share of the Buddha's relics.

timeline.event: Identified by Col. Deane and Aurel Stein

facts.text: Tradition says it was built by Uttarasena to enshrine relics.
facts.quote: It was built by Uttarasena, an ancient king of Swat, to enshrine his share of the relics of Buddha.

facts.text: It was identified by Deane and Stein.
facts.quote: The Shingardar stupa was identified by Colonel Deane and S.A Stein during the British period.

access: Just off the main road between Ghalegay and Barikot.

name: Swat Museum
summary: The archaeological museum of Swat on the Mingora-Saidu Sharif road, holding Gandharan sculpture, reliquaries and an ethnographic gallery. It was closed in the 2000s, its collection moved for safety, and a new earthquake-resistant building opened in December 2014.

timeline.event: Museum conceived by the Italian Archaeological Mission and the Wali of Swat
Badly damaged by the Kashmir earthquake
Closed during the conflict; contents moved to Taxila; a bomb exploded nearby in February 2008 and damaged the building
2,700 objects returned
New seismic-resistant museum opened

facts.text: The museum was conceived in 1959.
facts.quote: The museum was conceived in 1959 under the aegis of the Italian Archaeological Mission to Swat and the Wali of Swat

facts.text: A new building opened on 11 December 2014.
facts.quote: a new seismic-resistant museum was opened on December 11, 2014.

facts.text: Most holdings come from Butkara I and Odigram.
facts.quote: mostly from Butkara No 1 and Odigram

access: On the Mingora-Saidu Sharif road; open to visitors, check opening days locally.

name: White Palace, Marghazar
summary: White marble summer palace of Swat's first ruler, Miangul Abdul Wadud, built at Marghazar in the late 1930s-1941 and now a hotel. It hosted Queen Elizabeth II in 1961 and sits among large chinar trees below Elum Ghar.

timeline.event: Wadud decides to build a summer residence
Palace built and completed
Elizabeth II and Prince Philip stay three days

facts.text: It was built in 1940 of white marble by the first king of Swat.
facts.quote: The White Palace of Marghazar was built in 1940 by the first king of Swat, Miangul Abdul Wadud (Badshah Sahib)

facts.text: Elizabeth II and Prince Philip stayed three days in 1961.
facts.quote: stayed for three days in 1961

facts.text: The palace has a 200-year-old chinar tree.
facts.quote: There is also a 200-year-old colossal chinar tree

access: 13 km from Saidu Sharif on a paved hill road; year-round, cool in summer, hotel with day visits.

name: Bashigram Lake
summary: Alpine glacial lake east of Madyan, reached by jeep and hike from Bashigram village.

facts.text: It lies east of Madyan.
facts.quote: is an alpine glacial lake located to the eastern side of Madyan in Swat District

access: Jeep to Bashigram, then hike; summer.

name: Saidgai Lake
summary: High lake on the Swat/Upper Dir border northwest of Gabin Jabba, reached by long treks.

facts.text: It is at 3,500 m near the Dir-Swat border.
facts.quote: Saidgai Lake is close to the border between of Dir Upper and Swat.

access: Trek from Ushirai Dara (Dir, ~6 h) or Lalko; June-Aug.

name: Fizagat
summary: Riverside hill-station park on the Swat River just north of Mingora with a recreation park, popular for day trips.

facts.text: It is described as a popular hill station with a recreation park.
facts.quote: Fizagat or Hyatabad is a popular hill station located in Swat Valley of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan.

access: About 5 km north of Mingora on the Kalam road; year-round.

name: Gabin Jabba
summary: Forested meadow plateau in Matta tehsil, a jeep gateway to Daral and Saidgai lakes with bee-keeping and springs.

facts.text: Elevation is 2,582 m.
facts.quote: Gabin Jabba elevation is 2582 m (8471 ft) from the sea level.

facts.text: It serves as a gateway to Daral Lake.
facts.quote: Gabin Jabba serves as a gateway to the Daral Lake

access: 4WD from Lalko village; summer.

name: Jahanzeb College
summary: State-era college founded by Wali Miangul Jahanzeb in Saidu Sharif; one of the buildings of the princely-state period.

timeline.event: College founded

facts.text: Founded in 1952.
facts.quote: most notably Jehanzeb College in 1952

access: Saidu Sharif town; exterior viewing only (working college).

name: Jarogo Waterfall
summary: Tall cascade in the hills of Matta/Upper Dir listed among Swat attractions.

facts.text: Listed among Swat's waterfalls.
facts.quote: Jarogo Waterfall

access: Hike from nearby village; summer.

name: Lowari Pass (Lowari Top)
summary: High pass between Dir and Chitral, shut by snow roughly late November to May; the Lowari Tunnel now bypasses it.

facts.text: Closed by snow late November to May.
facts.quote: This closure typically extends from the latter part of November to the ending days of May each year.

facts.text: Lowest pass into Chitral.
facts.quote: Lowari Pass is a relatively low pass, by far the lowest pass to enter Chitral.

access: Old N-45 switchbacks above Dir; the tunnel is preferred in practice.

name: Lowari Tunnel
summary: Two-tube vehicular tunnel under Lowari Pass on N-45, 10.4 km combined length, the all-weather road to Chitral.

facts.text: Combined 10.4 km, under Lowari Pass.
facts.quote: consists of two separate tunnels, and the combined length of both tunnels is 10.4 kilometers (6.5 miles).

access: N-45 north of Dir.

name: Malakand Pass
summary: The pass on the Peshawar-Swat road (via Dargai and Batkhela) that opens the Swat region; site of the 1895 and 1897 fighting.

facts.text: Connects Peshawar with the Chitral District.
facts.quote: is a mountain pass in the Malakand District of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, that connects Peshawar with the Chitral District.

access: Dargai, the tunnel, then Batkhela on N-45/N-95.

name: Malam Jabba Ski Resort
summary: Pakistan's only ski resort outside Gilgit-Baltistan's Naltar, a hill station about 40 km from Saidu Sharif with a chairlift, an 800 m slope and a hotel. The resort was burned in 2008 during the conflict and rebuilt and reopened from 2016.

timeline.event: Resort destroyed in the Swat conflict
New 800 m chairlift inaugurated
Five-star Pearl-Continental hotel opened

facts.text: It is one of Pakistan's two ski resorts.
facts.quote: Malam Jabba is home to one of the two ski resorts in Pakistan

facts.text: The resort apex is 2,804 m.
facts.quote: the resort's apex rests at an elevation of 2804 m (9200 ft) above sea level

facts.text: The resort was destroyed in June 2008.
facts.quote: The resort was destroyed by Taliban militants in June 2008

facts.text: A new 800 m chairlift opened in September 2016.
facts.quote: A new 800 meter long ski chairlift was inaugurated in September 2016.

access: Paved road from Manglor (about 40 km from Saidu Sharif); chairlift and snow season Dec-Feb, summer for hiking.

name: Saidu Sharif Airport
summary: The Swat valley airport (IATA SDT, ICAO OPSS) between Kanju and Dherai; flights resumed in March 2021 after a 17-year hiatus.

facts.text: Built in 1978.
facts.quote: The airport was built in 1978

facts.text: Flights resumed in March 2021.
facts.quote: after a hiatus of 17 years, the flight operation at the airport resumed in March 2021.

facts.text: Used by visitors to Swat and Malam Jabba.
facts.quote: Visitors traveling to Swat Valley and the Malam Jabba ski resort during the summer season use this airport to reach Swat District.

access: About 5 km north of Saidu Sharif on Airport Road.

name: Shangla Pass
summary: Mountain pass on the Khwazakhela-Alpuri road between Swat and Shangla, offering views over lower Swat.
access: Paved road; year-round except heavy snow.
